# Knowledge map: Firmware dump sets and partition identity

<!-- Generated by `python -m tools.research.knowledge_map build` from `docs/map/sources/firmware-dumps.toml`. Do not edit by hand. -->

- **Scope:** The local ILCE-6100 and ILCE-6400 partition sets, their integrity against stored manifests, the build identity each set carries, and which partitions are byte-identical across the two bodies.
- **Evidence span:** see record index; last reviewed 2026-11-26.
- **Deep review:** 0 of 6 records read in full and checked claim by claim ([curation plan](CURATION_PLAN.md)); the rest are curated from titles, lead paragraphs and consolidated documents.
- **Status legend:** PHYSICAL = observed on the camera/host; OFFLINE = disassembly, Unicorn or static proof; INFERENCE = argued from evidence, not observed directly; RETRACTED/REFUTED = do not rely on, kept to prevent re-derivation.

The evidence records are authoritative; follow the links before acting on a claim.

## Frontier

### <a id="f01"></a>F01 - Acquisition provenance and a6100 partition roles

- **State:** `open`
- **Next:** Record the a6100 fetch conditions (service or normal mode, camera uptime, mount state) and read /proc/mounts read-only on the ILCE-6100 so its partition roles stop being inferred from the a6400; neither set is a whole-device image.
- **Evidence:** [E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md)

## Hazards (read before any camera run)

| ID | Hazard | Effect | Rule | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="h01"></a>H01 | Publishing or committing a dump set | The sets contain proprietary firmware plus live settings, serials and Wi-Fi configuration; committing or uploading them would leak private device data. | Keep dumps under the git-ignored `dumps/` directory, never commit, attach or publish them, and cite only hashes, sizes and build strings. | [E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md) |
| <a id="h02"></a>H02 | Refreshing a stored hash to silence a mismatch | A regenerated checksum would hide whether an image or a metadata file changed and destroy the capture's identity. | Investigate the mismatch and record it; never rewrite SHA256SUMS, manifest.json or manifest-final.json to make a check pass. | [E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md), [E0524](../evidence/0524-reproducible-captured-qemu-boot-and-liro-waits.md) |

## Entities

### <a id="source-a6100-dump"></a>ILCE-6100 Ver.1.00 partition set

`source.a6100-dump` | source

Fastboot fetch set of 19 nflasha images (1,361,051,648 bytes) with two passes from different fetch sessions and a 19/19 SHA-256 list.

Aliases: `a6100-dump-20261120`, `dumps/a6100-dump-20261120`, `38115_03.2021040601`

Current knowledge:

- **C01** `PHYSICAL` The ILCE-6100 fetch set is complete for its 19 listed images (1,361,051,648 bytes, 1,298 MiB): every partition has two passes from different fetch sessions, each pair agrees on SHA-256 and MD5, and all 19 entries in SHA256SUMS match. Session 2 ended on budget and was resumed; sessions 1, 3, 4 and 5 are complete. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md))
- **C03** `INFERENCE` The a6100 set is the dump E9101 examined: nflasha3 SHA-256 08379a20... matches it, and its bytes carry the build identity `Linux version 3.0.27_nl-rt106+` (dic-build-scm-354, 2021-04-06, Sony CE Linux 8.2.6.0) with nflasha7:/version.txt `38115_03.2021040601`. E9101 identifies that dump as ILCE-6100 Ver.1.00; the fetch manifest itself carries no model or version field, so the model name rests on that record, not on the bytes. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md), [E9101](../evidence/9101-a6100-picture-profile-gate.md))
- **C05** `OFFLINE` The two sets share one 18-partition size map (1,360,986,112 bytes each; the a6100 adds a 65,536-byte nflasha_head), and exactly three partitions are byte-identical: nflasha16 (146,800,640 bytes, all zero), nflasha23 (2,097,152 bytes) and nflashaB1 (4,194,304 bytes, all zero). The other 15 differ, including nflasha1, nflasha5, nflasha7 and nflasha15. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md))
- **C06** `OFFLINE` Observed formats in the a6100 set: FAT12 on nflasha1/2/3/6/10/12/13/18, FAT16 on nflasha11/17, ext2 on nflasha7 (1,216 inodes, 4,844 blocks) and nflasha15 (52,832 inodes, 211,164 blocks), WBI1 on nflasha5, an EXBL container on nflashaB0, an undecoded `CMMe` header on nflasha4, and all-zero nflasha16 and nflashaB1. nflasha7 carries 25 root names including version.txt; the a6100 adds tmp_ipsec to the a6400 set. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md))
- **C07** `INFERENCE` The shared nflasha23 bytes show the same 2 MiB partition content on both bodies, which is consistent with but does not attest the ILCE-6400A MSC LUN 1 backing that E0674 left unattested. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md))

### <a id="source-a6400-dump"></a>ILCE-6400 read-only partition set

`source.a6400-dump` | source

E0477 read-only capture of 18 nflasha partitions (1,360,986,112 bytes), a 1 MiB head read and three filesystem archives.

Aliases: `a6400-nflasha-readonly`, `dumps/a6400-nflasha-readonly`, `38111_06.2021081003`

Current knowledge:

- **C02** `PHYSICAL` The ILCE-6400 set holds 18 partition images (1,360,986,112 bytes) plus a 1 MiB head read and three filesystem archives. 38 of 39 SHA256SUMS.txt entries match; the only exception is the known manifest-final.json metadata mismatch first recorded in E0524, while every partition image and the head read match. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md), [E0524](../evidence/0524-reproducible-captured-qemu-boot-and-liro-waits.md), [E0414](../evidence/0414-nflasha-readonly-device-check-and-boot-area-dumps.md))
- **C04** `OFFLINE` The a6400 set is a distinct build of the same release: nflasha7:/version.txt reads `38111_06.2021081003`, and the captured kernel banner is dic-build-scm-348, 2021-08-10, Sony CE Linux 8.2.6.0. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md), [E0415](../evidence/0415-nflasha-boot-decode-and-full-emulation-roadmap.md))
- **C05** `OFFLINE` The two sets share one 18-partition size map (1,360,986,112 bytes each; the a6100 adds a 65,536-byte nflasha_head), and exactly three partitions are byte-identical: nflasha16 (146,800,640 bytes, all zero), nflasha23 (2,097,152 bytes) and nflashaB1 (4,194,304 bytes, all zero). The other 15 differ, including nflasha1, nflasha5, nflasha7 and nflasha15. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md))
- **C07** `INFERENCE` The shared nflasha23 bytes show the same 2 MiB partition content on both bodies, which is consistent with but does not attest the ILCE-6400A MSC LUN 1 backing that E0674 left unattested. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md))

### <a id="proc-dump-integrity"></a>Dump integrity and cross-body comparison

`proc.dump-integrity` | process

Recomputing each stored checksum, reading partition signatures and build strings, and comparing the same partition across bodies by SHA-256.

Aliases: `dump-inventory`, `sha256sum -c`

Current knowledge:

- **C01** `PHYSICAL` The ILCE-6100 fetch set is complete for its 19 listed images (1,361,051,648 bytes, 1,298 MiB): every partition has two passes from different fetch sessions, each pair agrees on SHA-256 and MD5, and all 19 entries in SHA256SUMS match. Session 2 ended on budget and was resumed; sessions 1, 3, 4 and 5 are complete. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md))
- **C02** `PHYSICAL` The ILCE-6400 set holds 18 partition images (1,360,986,112 bytes) plus a 1 MiB head read and three filesystem archives. 38 of 39 SHA256SUMS.txt entries match; the only exception is the known manifest-final.json metadata mismatch first recorded in E0524, while every partition image and the head read match. ([E0707](../evidence/0707-firmware-dump-sets-a6100-a6400.md), [E0524](../evidence/0524-reproducible-captured-qemu-boot-and-liro-waits.md), [E0414](../evidence/0414-nflasha-readonly-device-check-and-boot-area-dumps.md))
- **C05** `OFFLINE` The two sets share one 18-partition size map (1,360,986,112 bytes each; the a6100 adds a 65,536-byte nflasha_head), and exactly three partitions are byte-identical: nflasha16 (146,800,640 bytes, all zero), nflasha23 (2,097,152 bytes) and nflashaB1 (4,194,304 bytes, all zero).
